text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament amended the act on accounting late Tuesday.

- The Alliance of Free Democrats is to initiate a parliamentary hearing because the Prime Minister's Office failed to inform either Parliament or its coalition partner when it began background talks with Slovakia on the Gabcikovo hydroelectric power plant project.
- Young Democrat MPs criticised Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze Tuesday for his dismissal of four top police executives.
- Christian Democrat President Gyorgy Giczy convened a special meeting of the national board for December 14-15.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in his speech at the Lisbon summit of the OSCE that Hungary looks to the European Union and NATO for guarantees in the strengthening of its security, internal stability and economic advancement.
- Hungarian Premier Gyula Horn and newly elected Romanian President Emil Constantinescu held a meeting in Lisbon.
- The bus manufacturer Ikarus Rt. will close this year with losses of HUF 3.5 billion on sales of HUF 13.5 billion, said president Gabor Szeles.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Minister of Justice Pal Vastagh and his French counterpart Jacques Toubon agreed in Paris Tuesday that France would provide its expertise in translating some 50,000 pages of EU laws into Hungarian.

- Press attache at the Swiss Embassy in Budapest Bernhard Gasser said that the publishing of research by two Swiss historians into a 1973 Hungarian-Swiss agreement on assets rights may be delayed until December 16.
- The World Bank will not approve a $225 million loan scheme to be granted to Hungary earlier than mid-January, as opposed to the original deadline of a few weeks earlier.
- A special meeting of the national presidential board of the Socialist Party will be held on Thursday to discuss pending questions over government personnel.
- Border guard spokesman Attila Krisan firmly denied Austrian press reports that the green frontier between the two countries was easily crossed by on average more than 100 persons daily.
NEPSZAVA
- Parliament amended the nuclear act.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said that Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs is to participate at a joint meeting of ministers from NATO member countries and Partnership for Peace nations at the North Atlantic Cooperation Council session on December 11.
- A conference on refugees to be jointly sponsored by the office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees and Hungary's Interior Ministry will be staged in Budapest next April.
- Some 25,000-30,000 unemployed Hungarians have not received any benefits for two months and cannot expect to get any for the rest of the year.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Exports in November totalled $1.5 billion, an unprecedented monthly record in Hungary's history, president of the National Bank of Hungary told Reuters as reported in this paper.
- Hungary may achieve the fastest economic growth in Central and Eastern Europe over the next few decades, a report by the IMF reveals.
- The telephone company Ericsson Kft. will post sale of HUF 18 billion this year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
